messages:
mira: heads up — canary 1923 saw intermittent token tail latency spikes during low qps (~5 r/s). CPU on the kernel pod is fine but we're seeing long stalls correlated with KV miss bursts. attaching brief logs and a repro run below.

mira: log snippet: `2026-03-16T14:12:03Z kernel: stall_ms=138 enqueue_depth=32 kv_misses=47 ctx=decode`

mira: hypothesis: backpressure from KV miss path + batch head-of-line blocking. can we check any recent kv eviction/regression? @ana @kevin

kevin: looking. can you paste a flame or perf trace when it happened? I want to see if the stall is in the attention kernel waiting on I/O vs waiting on wakeup.

mira: attaching a short perf link: https://perf.redwood/internal/trace/0x9ab — note the flatline at 14:12:03 (3 samples) where threads are WAITING on futex.

ana: (note: name typo) — sorry, meant @ana.

ana: also bump — is the canary running quantized kernel or float? small quant changes can change concurrency behaviour.

ana: we saw an eviction spike in the same window: `kv.evictions.rate=22/s` and `kv.load_latency.p95=120ms`. we had a prefetch candidate enabled last deploy for long-seq workloads. could be interacting.

kevin: OK — two quick asks: 1) can you retest with prefetch disabled, 2) try kernel flag `--abort-on-stall=false` (we recently changed default). If stall goes away that's our clue.

sam: from infra side, capacity for canary was at min GPUs for the pool — if you hit a small ripple in QPS the batching window can change drastically. try set pool.min=1, pool.max=2 and run a 2min sustained to see behavior.

mira: running three quick experiments now: (A) prefetch OFF, (B) abort-on-stall=false, (C) bump pool.min to 1 (was 0). posting results in ~5m.

jen: quick reminder: please tag the canary id in the perf dashboard so perf-bot collects traces automatically: `#canary=1923` -> perf-bot will annotate.

perf-bot: noted — collecting traces for canary=1923 from 2026-03-16T14:10Z to 2026-03-16T14:20Z.

mira: experiment A results: prefetch OFF -> kv.load_latency.p95 down to 32ms, stall events dropped to 2 (from ~8). tail latency improved ~18%. seems promising.

mira: experiment B (abort-on-stall=false) — no significant change on its own. Batching still blocks on cache misses.

mira: experiment C (pool.min=1) — smoother batching windows, enqueue_depth max dropped from 32 to 12, stalls nearly eliminated in this run.

kevin: good info. suggests interaction between prefetch path and small-GPU-pool batching. next steps: kernel team to add a short-path for cache-miss fast-fail (non-blocking eviction fallback), kv team to tune prefetch heuristics for low-qps canaries.

ana: ack. we'll prepare a prefetch config toggle (threshold based on qps and seq-length) and push a draft PR.

kevin: I'll spin a small change to kernel to add `--miss-fastpath` that returns a placeholder token stream instead of blocking the batch. will run internal microbench first.

sam: ops note — we should avoid changing pool sizing live for prod canaries; recommend coord with release-manager before ramping. for canaries it's ok.

mira: thanks all. can each owner drop a one-line action in the PR: @kevin (kernel fastpath), @ana (prefetch threshold), @sam (canary sizing guidance). ping here when PRs are up. :thumbsup:
